title: Prince Sharma and 7 Others v. State of U.P. and another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J. and Vivek Kumar Singh, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; NPCL to redress connection grievance within four weeks.
headnote: Writ seeking a mandamus for 2 KW connections disposed of, without any opinion on the merits, with a consensual direction to the Vice President, NPCL, to look into the grievance and redress it within four weeks of production of a certified copy.
facts: In June 2022 Prince Sharma and seven others applied to Noida Power Company Limited for fresh 2 KW electricity connections on their respective plots. The connections remained unreleased, and in 2023 they petitioned the Allahabad High Court for a direction to grant them on payment of usual charges. They invoked section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and the stated liability of Rs.1,000 a day after one month. The State submitted that the Act and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 contain the remedy.

holding_units.topic: fresh-connection grievance left to the licensee
holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on the merits, and with the consent of the parties, the writ is disposed of with a direction to the Vice President, Noida Power Company Limited, Knowledge Park-IV, Greater Noida, to look into the petitioners' grievance for release of the 2 KW connections and to redress it within four weeks from production of a certified copy of the order.

principle_tags.application: The petitioners invoked the one-month duty under section 43. The Court expressed no opinion on that duty. In view of the submission that the Act and the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 are self-contained, and with the parties' consent, it directed the licensee to look into and redress the grievance within four weeks.

not_decided.point: Whether section 43 required NPCL to release the 2 KW connections within one month and attracted the stated per-day liability
not_decided.note: The Court disposed of the writ without expressing any opinion on the merits and left redress to the licensee.
